title: Regulatory conditions on compliance packaging
rule_summary: A pharmacy or pharmacist may use compliance packaging, including oral-liquid-single-dose, single-drug-single-dose and multi-drug-single-dose packaging, provided the pharmacy designates a space preventing cross-contamination, maintains policies and procedures for each type used covering cleaning, labeling, dispensing, hand hygiene, quarantine and reverse distribution, THE PACKAGING DOES NOT CONFLICT WITH THE USP-DI MONOGRAPH OR FDA-APPROVED LABELING, and THE MEDICATIONS ARE COMPATIBLE with the packaging components and with each other.
exam_relevance: Separates the Board's controlled-substance policy question from the regulation's own conditions. Product labeling and compatibility govern whatever the patient prefers.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

common_confusions: Reading the Schedule II/III maintenance-medication policy as the whole of the compliance packaging rule.
Overlooking that FDA-approved labeling or a USP-DI monograph can forbid repackaging outright, whatever the pharmacy's procedures say.
verification_notes: Read verbatim in the current official publication on 2026-08-20 during Batch 3 tranche B3-F under Issue #91. A fresh independent legal and full-bank realism audit is still required before release.
